reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's desire for the Hebrew people's wellbeing through the conditional covenant offered to Jeroboam: 'If you listen to all I command you and walk in My ways and do what is right in My eyes... then I will build you an established house.' The narrative structure—where obedience brings blessing and disobedience brings punishment—presupposes that Yahweh desires their prosperity. The warnings and prophetic rebukes themselves indicate God's corrective intent, suggesting His aim is to redirect the people toward the conditions necessary for their wellbeing. Even the punishments are framed as consequences meant to bring them back into proper relationship with God.
